$$

$$
\frac{12}{n(n-1)}=\frac{1}{11},

so $n(n-1)=132$. The positive consecutive integers with product 132 are 12 and 11, giving $n=12$. Therefore the correct option is C.

decisions.question_stem_preview: What is the value of the definite integral $$\int_{0.5}^{1} \frac{(x+1)^3}{x^5} \, dx \text{ ?}$$

set_fields.solution_reasoning:
First expand and divide by $x^5$:

$$
\frac{(x+1)^3}{x^5}=\frac{x^3+3x^2+3x+1}{x^5}=x^{-2}+3x^{-3}+3x^{-4}+x^{-5}.
$$

Each term is now a permitted power of $x$, so

$$
\int \left(x^{-2}+3x^{-3}+3x^{-4}+x^{-5}\right)\,dx=-x^{-1}-\frac{3}{2}x^{-2}-x^{-3}-\frac14x^{-4}.
$$

At $x=1$ this is $-\frac{15}{4}$. At $x=\frac12$ it is

$$
-2-6-8-4=-20.
$$

Therefore

$$
\int_{0.5}^{1}\frac{(x+1)^3}{x^5}\,dx=-\frac{15}{4}-(-20)=\frac{65}{4}.
$$

The correct option is A.

replacement_question.subject: Biology
replacement_question.question_stem:
In pea plants, the allele for purple flowers, $P$, is dominant to the allele for white flowers, $p$. A pure-breeding purple plant is crossed with a pure-breeding white plant. Two plants from the resulting $F_1$ generation are then crossed.

A purple-flowered plant is chosen at random from the $F_2$ generation and crossed with a white-flowered plant. What is the probability that their first offspring has white flowers?
replacement_question.solution_reasoning:
The first cross is $PP\times pp$, so every $F_1$ plant is $Pp$. The $F_1$ cross is therefore $Pp\times Pp$, giving $F_2$ genotype probabilities

$$
PP:\ Pp:\ pp=\frac14:\frac12:\frac14.
$$

A purple $F_2$ plant is either $PP$ or $Pp$. Conditional on being purple,

$$
P(Pp\mid\text{purple})=\frac{1/2}{3/4}=\frac23.
$$

Only a $Pp$ plant can produce a white offspring when crossed with $pp$, and that cross gives a white offspring with probability $1/2$. Hence

$$
\frac23\times\frac12=\frac13.
$$

The correct option is D.
replacement_question.solution_key_insight: Condition on the selected F2 plant being purple before applying the test cross.

distractor_map.C: Uses the F2 probability of white flowers rather than the probability in the test cross.
distractor_map.E: Assumes every purple F2 plant is heterozygous.
distractor_map.F: Finds the probability that the chosen purple plant is heterozygous but does not include the 1/2 chance of a white offspring.

set_fields.question_stem:
A quadratic function $f$ has its stationary point at $x=2$.
A second function is $g(x)=(x-2)^2+1$, and $H(x)=f(g(x))$.

Because $f$ is quadratic with stationary point at input 2, write

$$
f(t)=a(t-2)^2+c.
$$

Now $g(1)=2$, so

$$
H(1)=f(2)=c=10.
$$

Also $g(2)=1$, so

$$
H(2)=f(1)=a+10=8,
$$

giving $a=-2$. Hence

$$
H(x)=10-2\bigl(g(x)-2\bigr)^2\le 10.
$$

The value 10 is attained when $g(x)=2$, for example at $x=1$ or $x=3$. Therefore the maximum is 10, option E.
